newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London fell sharply in reaction to lower values in the New York raw sugar market and knock-on white premium selling. By the close the benchmark December contract was down $5.40 at $327.00 a tonne while March fell $4.60 to $327.80. Overall volume totalled 3,603 lots, dominated by the two front positions. Technical analysts now believe that the weak London market is due for an upside correction given that values had moved into oversold territory.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended a heavily traded session lower across the board, but trade scale-down buying held the October contract above nearby support and buoyed prices off the lows by the close, market sources said. The bulk of the day's losses came after October sank through support at 11.50 cents/lb on early speculative liquidation. After hitting a low of 11.30, the contract consolidated and gradually retraced some losses ending at 11.43 cents/lb. The early selling also weighed heavily on the most active March contract, which fell to 11.28 cents/lb after being traded between 11.29 and 11.31. Additional selling is likely to come into the March contract since speculators have already rolled a hefty number of positions from October, ahead of the contract's expiry later this month, dealers said.

BRAZIL - Brazil's sugar campaign is remaining well on course for another record. Total production in August 1996 amounted to a massive 2.346 million tonnes, sharply up on last year's 1.974 million tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first four months of 1996/97 (May/August) to 7.216 million tonnes compared to 5.687 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total production in 1995/96 amounted to 13.636 million tonnes against 12.598 million in 1994/95. The steep increase in the first month of 1996/97 can be attributed to two factors, namely the higher cane crop in the Centre/South and the earlier than usual start to the campaign in both growing regions, the Centre/South and the North/Northeast. Usually factories in the North/Northeast start crushing in September but this year some started producing earlier, contributing 136,400 tonnes to the August total.

UNITED KINGDOM - Following recent dry weather sugar content of the 1996 beet crop now approaches average values while root weight developed sluggishly. Root weight amounted to 608 grams, up on last year's 516 grams but down on the 1991/95 average of 613 grams. Sugar content reached 17.23 percent, up from last year's 15.86 per cent and almost on par with the average of 17.27 percent. This resulted in a sugar weight per root of 104.8 grams against 88.8 grams in 1995 but still down on the average of 105.9 grams. A spokesman for British Sugar said the crop continued to make good progress although more rain was needed.

TURKEY - Atest beet test results from Turkey taken on August 15 suggest that the crop has improved greatly over the past few weeks with root weight now slightly above last year's results. Root weight on August 15 amounted to 34.80 tonnes, up from last year's 33.46 tonnes. Sugar content increased to 14.0 percent, unchanged from the previous year. This resulted in a theoretical sugar weight of 4.7 tonnes per ha, 4.3 percent up on 1995. Given the sharp increase in Turkey's area sown to beet the local industry is confident output will hit around 2 million tonnes in raw value terms, up from last year's 1.5 million tonnes.

BULGARIA - The latest beet test results of September 5 continue to be disappointing. Beet yield amounted to no more than 22.5 tonnes, down from last year's 49.0 tonnes and significantly below the five-year average (1991/95) of 42.4 tonnes. Sugar content was 15.9 percent, unchanged against the 1995 value and the average. This resulted in a sugar yield per ha of 3.6 tonnes, white value, almost 54 percent less than the 1995 result of 7.8 tonnes and also sharply below the average of 6.7 tonnes. As the 1996 beet area dropped sharply sugar production will probably be reduced to no more than 7,000 tonnes.

Tunisia bought one cargo of 14,000 tonnes of white sugar at $366.00 c&f, per tonne at a snap tender on Monday, traders said. Delivery is for April 1997. The state-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp is expected within weeks to tender for a three year contract for delivery of 60,000 tonnes of sugar a year, local traders said. Taiwan Sugar is likely to hold the invitation-only tender in New York within a few weeks, but exact dates have not been set. Taiwan Sugar bought two 30,000 tonne shipments of sugar on June 26 and is on track to import a total of 120,000 tonnes of sugar in 1996.
